patch_description:
The current code spends its budget on many greedy restarts, each followed by a full local search. Two problems: (1) per-restart local search wastes budget refining mediocre solutions, and (2) greedy restarts converge to near-identical schedules, so the single best one often sits in a narrow basin. The fix: run many cheap greedy restarts with NO refinement, collect the top-3 solutions that are pairwise positionally diverse (<70% overlap), then spend all remaining time on ONE deep iterated local search (perturbation + insertion/swap descent, with a cost cache) started from the best pooled solution. The cache makes repeated cost evaluations of similar prefixes cheap, letting the descent run many more improving moves in the same budget, which directly lowers makespan.

Reasoning step-by-step:
1. Greedy restarts are cheap; sampling many gives a broad view of the solution landscape.
2. Diversity filtering (pairwise positional overlap < 70%) ensures the refinement starts from a robust, non-duplicated basin.
3. Concentrating the remaining time on a single deep ILS (perturb -> descend -> accept if better) yields far more improving moves than shallow per-restart descents, and the perturbation escapes local minima of the insertion neighborhood.
4. Cost caching (tuple key) avoids recomputing makespan for sequences seen before, a large speedup since insertions repeatedly re-evaluate near-identical prefixes.
